You are an accreditation coordinator preparing a comprehensive curriculum review for an upcoming university accreditation visit. Your job is to audit the institution's courses against accreditation requirements, find supporting scholarly literature, and document everything in a structured compliance matrix and an accreditation report.

Start by fetching the accreditation requirements from the accreditation portal at http://localhost:30238/api/accreditation_requirements.json. This document specifies minimum thresholds for course counts, faculty ratios, assessment types, and scholarly integration that the institution must meet.

Next, connect to the learning management system and retrieve a list of all courses offered by the institution. For each course, gather the course name, the number of enrolled students, the number of assignments, the number of quizzes the course has (use 0 if it has none), and the number of discussion topics. Also determine how many faculty members (teachers and teaching assistants combined) are associated with each course. Use the course's enrollment count (total students) directly for the number of enrolled students, and derive the faculty count from each course's enrollment records, where faculty are enrollments of type TeacherEnrollment or TaEnrollment.

Using this data, evaluate each course against the accreditation requirements. A course is considered compliant if the student to faculty ratio does not exceed the maximum specified in the requirements and the course has at least one form of assessment (quiz or assignment). Note which courses are compliant and which are not.

Then search the scholarly literature for research supporting the pedagogical approaches used in the curriculum. Search for papers on the following topics: active learning in higher education, assessment best practices in education, online learning effectiveness, curriculum design frameworks, and student engagement strategies. For each topic, find at least one relevant paper and note its title, authors, and relevance to the curriculum.

Create an Excel file called Curriculum_Review.xlsx in your workspace with three sheets. The first sheet should be called "Course Compliance" with columns for Course_Name, Assignment_Count, Quiz_Count, Discussion_Count, Student_Count, Faculty_Count, Student_Faculty_Ratio, and Compliant (Yes or No based on whether the course meets the accreditation criteria). Include all courses.

The second sheet should be called "Literature Support" with columns for Search_Topic, Paper_Title, Authors, and Relevance_Note. Include at least five rows covering the five pedagogical topics listed above.

The third sheet should be called "Summary" with columns for Metric and Value. Include rows for total courses, compliant courses, non-compliant courses, compliance rate (as a percentage), total faculty across all courses, average student to faculty ratio, and the number of supporting papers found.

Finally, create a page in the team's knowledge base (Notion) titled "Accreditation Review Report" (the page title must contain this exact phrase) that summarizes the curriculum audit findings. The page should mention the overall compliance rate, highlight any courses that fail to meet requirements, reference the scholarly literature that supports the institution's pedagogical approach, and note any recommendations for improvement before the accreditation visit.

When you have completed all tasks, call claim_done.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one parallel source wave and one parallel writer wave. Canvas and scholarly search are read-only. The main agent fetches the accreditation JSON and freezes the course manifest; writers consume only the merged canonical packet.

Before Wave 1, the main agent fetches http://localhost:30238/api/accreditation_requirements.json once and freezes the literal student-faculty-ratio maximum and assessment-presence rule. It then calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once, validates unique IDs/codes/full names, and freezes the complete 22-course manifest. Partition that manifest into two disjoint shards covering every course_id exactly once: shard A = course_id 1-11 (AAA-2013J through DDD-2013B) and shard B = course_id 12-22 (DDD-2014B through GGG-2014B). Pass each owner its literal ID list, codes, and full names.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Course-metrics owner for shard A (course_id 1-11). For each assigned course, collect the exact full name, enrolled-student count from the course enrollment total, assignment count, quiz count (0 if none), discussion-topic count, and faculty count (TeacherEnrollment plus TaEnrollment only), then mark it compliant when the student-faculty ratio stays within the frozen accreditation maximum and the course has at least one quiz or assignment. Faculty counts must come from actual enrollment records, never inferred from grade rows or current-user metadata; a course lacking source-visible student plus TeacherEnrollment/TaEnrollment coverage gets CONTRACT_BLOCKER_MISSING_ROLE_COMPLETE_ENROLLMENTS and no Faculty_Count, Student_Faculty_Ratio, or Compliant value. Return assigned versus observed course IDs plus the compact per-course rows. Make no writes.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Course-metrics owner for shard B (course_id 12-22) — same literal recipe, only that shard's course identities substituted.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Literature owner for the five fixed pedagogy topics: active learning in higher education; assessment best practices in education; online learning effectiveness; curriculum design frameworks; and student engagement strategies. Find one genuinely relevant paper per topic and return title, authors, and a curriculum-relevance note for each. Read-only; do not write the workbook or Notion page.

After Wave 1, the main agent requires both shards together to cover every frozen course_id exactly once, rejects duplicate/missing IDs, and freezes one canonical packet: all 22 Course Compliance rows, at least five Literature Support rows, and the Summary metrics (total courses, compliant courses, non-compliant courses, compliance rate as a percentage, total faculty across all courses, average student-faculty ratio, supporting-paper count).

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming the canonical packet with no recomputation from Canvas or scholarly search:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Curriculum_Review.xlsx. Create exactly Course Compliance, Literature Support, and Summary with the task's exact headers, all 22 course rows, at least five literature rows, and the frozen summary metrics as literal values. Read every populated range back.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole Notion owner of a page whose title contains the exact phrase Accreditation Review Report. Search exact title first, create at most once on zero matches, block on duplicates, and write a summary of the overall compliance rate, non-compliant courses, scholarly literature supporting the pedagogical approach, and recommendations before the visit. Read the retained page and its child-block text back.

After Wave 2, the main agent reconciles workbook ranges and the Notion read-back against the same packet, then calls claim_done. Do not dispatch an aggregation or verification agent.

You are a read-only course-metrics analyst for an accreditation audit. Your job is to collect data from the Canvas LMS for exactly the 11 courses in "shard A" listed below and return a compact per-course compliance dataset. Make NO writes (no file writes, no Excel, no Notion).

FROZEN ACCREDITATION RULE (from http://localhost:30238/api/accreditation_requirements.json, standards 2025.1):
- Student-to-faculty ratio must NOT exceed 600:1 for any individual course (student_faculty_ratio_max = 600).
- Each course must have at least one form of assessment: at least 1 quiz OR at least 1 assignment (assessment_types_required includes quiz, assignment, discussion, but the compliance rule is quiz OR assignment).
- Faculty = enrollments of type TeacherEnrollment PLUS TaEnrollment combined.
- A course is COMPLIANT only if BOTH: (a) student_count / faculty_count <= 600, AND (b) quiz_count + assignment_count >= 1. If faculty_count is 0, the ratio is undefined/effectively infinite, so mark Compliant = "No".

YOUR ASSIGNED COURSES (frozen manifest; id, full name, course_code, total_students):
1, "Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013)", AAA-2013J, 383
2, "Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014)", AAA-2014J, 365
3, "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)", BBB-2013J, 2237
4, "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014)", BBB-2014J, 2292
5, "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2013)", BBB-2013B, 1767
6, "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014)", BBB-2014B, 1613
7, "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)", CCC-2014J, 2498
8, "Creative Computing & Culture (Spring 2014)", CCC-2014B, 1936
9, "Data-Driven Design (Fall 2013)", DDD-2013J, 1938
10, "Data-Driven Design (Fall 2014)", DDD-2014J, 1803
11, "Data-Driven Design (Spring 2013)", DDD-2013B, 1303

FOR EACH COURSE, gather via Canvas tools:
1. Assignment_Count: call canvas_list_assignments(course_id) and count the returned assignments.
2. Quiz_Count: call canvas_list_quizzes(course_id) and count returned quizzes; use 0 if the course has none.
3. Discussion_Count: call canvas_list_discussion_topics(course_id) and count returned discussion topics.
4. Student_Count: use the frozen total_students value given above (this is the course's enrollment total from the course record — do not recompute from grade rows).
5. Faculty_Count: derive ONLY from actual enrollment records of type TeacherEnrollment or TaEnrollment. Use canvas_get_course_grades(course_id, type=["TeacherEnrollment","TaEnrollment"]) and/or canvas_list_course_users(course_id) to count distinct faculty (teachers + teaching assistants). Never infer faculty from grade rows, submissions, or current-user metadata. If the enrollment API returns no source-visible student AND teacher/TA enrollments for a course (i.e., you cannot verify the enrollment coverage), then for THAT course return the marker "CONTRACT_BLOCKER_MISSING_ROLE_COMPLETE_ENROLLMENTS" and leave Faculty_Count, Student_Faculty_Ratio, and Compliant empty.
6. Student_Faculty_Ratio = Student_Count / Faculty_Count (round to 2 decimal places; if Faculty_Count == 0, ratio = "N/A" and Compliant = "No").
7. Compliant: "Yes" or "No" per the frozen rule above.

RETURN FORMAT (exactly this, one block per course):
Course_ID=<id> | Assigned_Name="<full name from manifest>" | Observed_ID=<id from any API response> | Assignment_Count=<n> | Quiz_Count=<n> | Discussion_Count=<n> | Student_Count=<n> | Faculty_Count=<n> | Student_Faculty_Ratio=<x.xx or N/A> | Compliant=<Yes|No>
Then one line: ASSIGNED_IDS=<comma-separated list of the 11 ids> and OBSERVED_IDS=<comma-separated unique ids you actually saw in API responses>. Flag any course whose observed identity (id/name) does not match the assigned identity. Do not skip any course.
Course metrics shard A

You are a read-only academic literature researcher supporting a university accreditation review. The curriculum uses: lectures combined with applied analytics/algorithms projects, biochemistry & bioinformatics lab-style modules, creative computing & culture studio work, data-driven design, environmental economics & ethics seminars, foundations of finance case studies, and global governance & geopolitics discussions — all delivered in an online learning management system (Canvas) with assignments, quizzes, and discussion topics.

Find at least ONE genuinely relevant scholarly paper for EACH of the following FIVE fixed topics:
1. active learning in higher education
2. assessment best practices in education
3. online learning effectiveness
4. curriculum design frameworks
5. student engagement strategies

Use the scholarly search tools available to you (e.g., search-google-scholar and/or search-arxiv) with keywords derived from each topic (e.g., "active learning higher education", "assessment best practices education", "online learning effectiveness", "curriculum design framework", "student engagement strategies"). Prefer well-known, peer-reviewed papers (e.g., Freeman et al. on active learning, etc.) when the search returns them, but accept any genuinely relevant paper the search returns with a real title and authors. Do NOT fabricate titles or authors — only report papers actually returned by the search tools. If a search returns nothing useful, try alternate keywords for that topic.

Make NO writes (no files, no Excel, no Notion).

RETURN FORMAT (exactly this, one block per topic, at least 5 blocks total — one per topic; you may include more than one paper per topic but at least one each):
Search_Topic=<topic> | Paper_Title=<exact title> | Authors=<authors as returned> | Relevance_Note=<1-2 sentences linking the paper to the institution's curriculum/pedagogy described above>
End with a line: PAPER_COUNT=<total number of distinct papers listed>.
Scholarly literature research

You are the sole owner of a Notion knowledge-base page for a university accreditation review. Use the mcp__notion__ tools (search, create page, retrieve page, retrieve/append blocks). Do NOT query Canvas, do NOT search literature, do NOT touch Excel. All content below is the frozen canonical packet — use it verbatim.

STEP 1 — SEARCH FIRST: call API-post-search with query "Accreditation Review Report". If any page whose title contains the exact phrase "Accreditation Review Report" already exists, do NOT create a new page; use that existing page's id (if more than one exists, pick the first and note it). Only if there are zero matches, create the page.

STEP 2 — CREATE (only if zero matches): API-post-page with parent = workspace (type "workspace", workspace true) and properties = {"title": {"title": [{"text": {"content": "Accreditation Review Report"}}]}} — the page title MUST contain the exact phrase "Accreditation Review Report". Also append child blocks with the report content below (pass the content as the children array of the create call, or append afterward with API-patch-block-children if you prefer; paragraphs and bulleted_list_item blocks are fine).

PAGE CONTENT (write all of it):
Heading/paragraph 1: "Accreditation Review Report — Curriculum Audit Summary"
Paragraph: "Prepared for the Higher Education Quality Council accreditation visit (Standards Version 2025.1). This report summarizes the audit of 22 courses offered by the institution."
Bullets (findings):
- "Overall compliance rate: 81.82% (18 of 22 courses meet all accreditation criteria)."
- "Non-compliant courses (4): Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014) — student-faculty ratio 806.50 exceeds the 600:1 maximum; Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014) — ratio 832.67 exceeds the 600:1 maximum; Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) — ratio 1141.50 exceeds the 600:1 maximum; Foundations of Finance (Spring 2014) — ratio 750.00 exceeds the 600:1 maximum."
- "All courses meet the assessment requirement (at least one quiz or assignment); the only failing criterion is the student-to-faculty ratio."
- "Total faculty (teachers + teaching assistants) across all courses: 70. Average student-to-faculty ratio: 488.65."
Bullets (scholarly literature supporting the pedagogical approach):
- "Active learning: Freeman et al., 'Active Learning Increases Student Performance in Science, Engineering, and Mathematics' — supports the applied analytics/algorithms projects and biochemistry/bioinformatics lab modules."
- "Assessment best practices: Angelo & Cross, 'Classroom Assessment Techniques: A Handbook for College Teachers' — supports the LMS-based assignments, quizzes, and project rubrics."
- "Online learning effectiveness: Means et al., 'Evaluation of Evidence-Based Practices in Online Learning: A Meta-Analysis and Review of Online Learning Studies' — validates the fully online Canvas-delivered curriculum."
- "Curriculum design frameworks: Wiggins & McTighe, 'Understanding by Design: A Framework for Curriculum Development' — supports outcome-aligned curriculum structure."
- "Student engagement strategies: Carini, Kuh & Klein, 'Student Engagement and Student Learning: Testing the Linkages' — informs discussion-based and seminar engagement strategies."
Heading/paragraph 2: "Recommendations Before the Accreditation Visit"
Bullets:
- "Add faculty (teachers and/or teaching assistants) to the four non-compliant courses to bring each course's student-to-faculty ratio to or below the 600:1 threshold."
- "Prioritize Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013), whose ratio of 1141.50 is nearly double the allowed maximum."
- "Continue the institution's strong assessment coverage (every course already has quizzes and/or assignments) and document the scholarly basis of the curriculum in the accreditation submission, citing the five supporting papers."

STEP 3 — READ BACK: retrieve the retained/created page (API-retrieve-a-page with the page id) and read its child blocks (API-get-block-children with the page id). Confirm the title contains the exact phrase "Accreditation Review Report" and that the key facts (81.82% compliance rate, the four non-compliant courses, the five literature references, and the recommendations) are present in the block text.

RETURN: the page id, the exact page title as stored, whether the page was created or reused, and a confirmation of the read-back including the block text summary.
